name: Palacio de los Gobernadores (Palace of the Governors)
aka: El Palacio Real de Santa Fe

dates.altered: The survey records seventy-five feet of the west end collapsed in 1853, a Victorian portal added between 1866 and 1883, and a rehabilitation for museum purposes begun in 1909 under Jesse L. Nusbaum that restored the portal 'to a more primitive' form. Both style nodes' exemplar notes say the famous portal is a 1909-13 reconstruction and not colonial fabric.
dates.note: The 1930s survey prints 'Between 1610 and 1614. (?)' with its own question mark; the Wikipedia infobox prints 'Built 1610'; both style nodes give 1610, and the new-mexico-adobe node adds substantial construction c. 1618-25 and a 1731 rebuilding after the Pueblo Revolt. Recorded as the survey states it; nothing edited to agree.
